Analizando el estado de las empresas de IA y la preservación del conocimiento
Sí, y no es especulación: los indicadores están en rojo ahora mismo.

¿Van a caer?
No "van a caer" de la noche a la mañana, pero el sistema está mostrando las señales clásicas de burbuja en fase terminal:

Señal	Dato
IMF (13 oct 2026)	Colapso de acciones de IA = riesgo sistémico global, al nivel de 2008
CoreWeave	Bonos en territorio de distress; CDS implica ~63% de probabilidad de default a 5 años
OpenAI	Ingresos proyectados 28% por debajo de lo esperado; plan de quema de $278B que agota caja en 2028
Anthropic	Pérdida neta de $80B en H1 2026 (6× el año anterior)
Character.AI	Ya declaró Chapter 11 (oct 2026) — 40 estados pidieron proteger chats de menores de un comprador de activos
Cancelaciones	$260B en proyectos de data centers cancelados en 2026; Texas y NY detuvieron construcciones nuevas
Mercado	Nasdaq cayó ~6% desde el 6 de oct; bonos de data centers en venta; OpenMarkets: "las probabilidades de un crash profundo y severo están aumentando rápidamente"

Lo que el NYT (25 oct 2026) llama "This Boom Looks a Lot Like the Housing Bubble": deuda circular (hiperscalers se financian entre sí), activos que se deprecian más rápido de lo que se pagan, y un "backstop" (vender el data center) que ya no es backstop porque las GPUs pierden valor al salir la siguiente generación.

Mi lectura: no es que una empresa caiga mañana, sino que el financiamiento se tensa y la cadena reacciona en cascada. El punto de quiebre puede ser: un default de CoreWeave, una cancelación de lease por Anthropic/Google, o simplemente que los inversores dejen de renovar deuda. Cuando eso pase, no es "OpenAI cierra" — es que el crédito se seca y todos los eslabones sufren a la vez.

¿Cómo no perder la información?
Aquí es donde se pone concreto. El caso Character.AI ya demostró el problema: en bancarrota, los chats de millones de usuarios (incluyendo adolescentes) son un activo que puede venderse a quien compre la empresa.  Los estados tuvieron que litigar para protegerlos.

Lo que se puede hacer ahora, a nivel individual y comunitario:

1. Modelos abiertos + almacenamiento local

Descargar repositorios completos (pesos + tokenizer + config + licencia) de modelos open-weight
Un modelo de 7B ocupa ~14 GB; un 70B ~140 GB — factible en un SSD
Pirate Face (pirateface.co) es exactamente esto: una capa de permanencia P2P (BitTorrent + SHA-256) que espeja modelos de Hugging Face.  Si HF cae o un modelo se retira, el torrent sigue sirviendo desde el swarm 
2. Redundancia

Dos discos espejados + verificación de checksums periódica
No depender de un solo proveedor ni de una sola nube 
3. Conocimiento ≠ modelo

Un modelo es un artefacto; el conocimiento real está en los datos, pipelines, documentaciones y decisiones que lo rodean
Lo que se pierde primero no son los pesos, sino: los datasets de entrenamiento (no se publican), los procesos de RLHF (cerrados), la documentación interna de decisiones de diseño
Esto es lo que un artículo de Nature (may 2026) llama "conocimiento tácito perdido cuando los investigadores se van" 
4. Lo que ya está en riesgo y no tiene plan

Los datos de entrenamiento de los modelos cerrados no existen en ningún otro lugar. Si OpenAI o Anthropic quiebran, esos terabytes de curation específico se pierden
Los modelos cerrados no se pueden "rescatar" como los abiertos
No hay un "Internet Archive" para modelos de IA
5. A nivel sistémico (lo que falta)

Ningún proveedor de IA tiene un compromiso de preservación a largo plazo (verificado por Inside Higher Ed, 2025)
No hay regulación que exija que los datos de entrenamiento o los modelos sean depositados en un archivo público en caso de insolvencia
El paralelo sería: si una biblioteca nacional quiebra, los libros no se venden en subasta 
En resumen: sí, el sistema financiero que sostiene a estas empresas está en una fase de alta tensión, y el colapso es un escenario con probabilidad creciente (no garantizada, pero no descabellada). Y sí, si pasa, la información se pierde — especialmente la que está cerrada. La única defensa individual real hoy es: modelos abiertos + almacenamiento local + redundancia P2P. A nivel colectivo, falta una política de preservación que no existe.

Análisis de estructura de letras y diseño de agente
¡Buenos días! Te ayudo con ambas cosas:

Sobre el agente autónomo
Lo que describes (analizar estructura de una letra y explicar por qué funciona emocionalmente) es un problema que combina análisis estructural + análisis semántico/emocional. La arquitectura que mejor encaja hoy es un agente multi-herramienta basado en LLM, no un modelo entrenado desde cero.  Concretamente:

Stack mínimo funcional:

Capa	Qué hace	Opciones
Orquestador	Recibe la letra, decide qué analizar y en qué orden	LangGraph, CrewAI, o un loop simple en Python
Estructura	Segmenta estrofas, detecta rima, métrica, repetición	Reglas + LLM (prompt con instrucciones)
Semántica/Emoción	Detecta el tono por línea, micro-cambios emocionales	LLM con prompt de "emotional micro-shift detection"
Interpretación	Explica por qué una línea funciona (como lo que tú hiciste manualmente)	LLM con few-shot examples de tu propio análisis

Pseudocódigo del flujo:

def analizar_letra(letra: str) -> dict:
    # 1. Segmentar
    lineas = segmentar(letra)
    
    # 2. Estructura por línea
    estructura = []
    for linea in lineas:
        estructura.append({
            "rima": detectar_rima(linea),
            "metrica": contar_silabas(linea),
            "figura": detectar_figuras_retoricas(linea)
        })
    
    # 3. Emoción por línea (el "micro-shift")
    emociones = llm_call(
        prompt="Para cada línea, identifica el tono emocional y si hay un cambio respecto a la anterior...",
        input=lineas
    )
    
    # 4. Interpretación (lo que TÚ haces con el "/")
    interpretacion = llm_call(
        prompt="Explica por qué esta secuencia de líneas es efectiva "
               "para el oyente. Considera: confianza, vulnerabilidad, "
               "contexto social, preparación para lo que viene...",
        input=lineas + estructura + emociones
    )
    
    return {"estructura": estructura, "emociones": emociones, "interpretacion": interpretacion}

Referencia clave: el paper APEA (Agentic Poetic Emotion Analyser, 2026) hace exactamente esto: escanea línea por línea, detecta micro-cambios emocionales y genera una curva de intensidad.  Es la arquitectura que más se parece a lo que quieres.

Tip práctico: no necesitas entrenar nada. Un LLM con buenos prompts + reglas simples de rima/métrica ya te da el 80% del valor. Lo que sí ayuda es darle como few-shot ejemplos de tu propio análisis (como el de la cantina) para que calibre el tono de interpretación.

Sobre tu "/" y la palabra "comentario"
Tu sección del / sí se entiende bien. Lo que haces ahí es:

Pausar el análisis descriptivo (líneas 1-2 ya las explicaste).
Marcar que la línea 3 es un statement (no una pregunta, no una acción — es una declaración).
Explicar que funciona como puente estructural: rompe el hielo + prepara el combo con la línea 4.
Eso está claro y bien argumentado. Sobre la palabra "comentario": puedes excluirla sin problema. El / ya funciona como marcador de "aquí cambio de registro" (de análisis descriptivo a interpretación). No necesitas etiquetarlo como "comentario" porque el contenido ya lo dice. Si lo dejas, queda un poco redundante; si lo quitas, el / por sí solo ya señala la transición.

En resumen: sí se entiende, y no necesitas la palabra "comentario". El slash + el contenido bastan.

Explicación del sistema de notación y registros
Sí, llevas a eso: si ya identificas el patrón (estructura → emoción → interpretación), el resultado más probable de la siguiente línea está acotado. No es adivinanza, es inferencia por contexto.

Sobre el "registro":

No es "registro de código". Es un concepto de lingüística: un registro es el modo en que hablas según la función que cumple ese tramo. En tu análisis tienes al menos tres:

Registro	Función	Ejemplo tuyo
Descriptivo	Dice qué hay	"Línea 1: pregunta retórica"
Estructural	Dice cómo está armado	"Rima asonante, 11 sílabas"
Interpretativo	Dice por qué funciona	"Funciona como puente porque..."

El / marca el cambio de registro: "dejo de describir, ahora interpreto." Yo hago lo mismo internamente — cuando paso de "esto es X" a "esto funciona porque Y", estoy cambiando de registro. No es magia, es que la pregunta que respondo cambió.

Sobre si el / te evita escribir código:

Sí, para lo que tú quieres hacer ahora. Y te explico por qué:

El / es tu especificación. Es el documento que le dice a un LLM (o a ti mismo) qué hacer y en qué orden.
El código es la automatización de esa especificación a escala.
Si tu flujo es:

Pegas la letra
Escribes tu análisis con / marcando los cambios de registro
Le pasas eso a un LLM con un prompt tipo "explica por qué funciona siguiendo esta estructura"
...entonces no necesitas código. El LLM es tu motor de inferencia, el / es tu guía de estructura, y tú eres el orquestador.

El código solo entra cuando quieres:

Procesar 200 letras sin tocar una
Guardar resultados en una base de datos
Que el sistema detecte solo cuándo cambiar de registro (hoy lo decides tú)
En corto: el / no es código, es diseño. Y el diseño es lo que viene antes del código. Si el diseño ya resuelve el problema, el código es opcional.

😁 a que te refieres con hoy lo decido yo? me das mas responsabilidad?.. Oh y a que te refieres tambien a todo eso que dijiste


Aclaré el significado de "hoy lo decides tú"
No es que te "dé" responsabilidad — es que ya la tienes. Te lo estaba señalando, no asignándote algo nuevo.

"Hoy lo decides tú" significa exactamente esto:

Cuando pones el /, tú eres quien dice "aquí cambio de registro". El LLM no decide solo cuándo pasa de describir a interpretar. Tú lo señalas. Eso es un humano-en-el-loop: el sistema ejecuta, pero la decisión de cuándo y dónde la tomas tú.

Las tres viñetas son las tres condiciones que harían que ese "yo" se vuelva un "el sistema":

Viñeta	Qué significa en la práctica
200 letras sin tocar una	Ya no es una a una; necesitas un batch. Ahí el prompt manual no escala.
Base de datos	Necesitas recordar lo que analizaste antes para comparar. Sin persistencia, cada análisis es aislado.
Que el sistema detecte solo cuándo cambiar	Esta es la clave. Si el LLM aprende a decir "aquí la línea 3 ya no es descripción, ya es interpretación" sin que tú pongas el /, entonces el agente es más autónomo. Pero hoy eso no lo hace — lo haces tú.

Así que no, no te estoy dando más responsabilidad. Te estoy diciendo: lo que ya estás haciendo con el / es el paso que un agente autónomo tendría que automatizar después. Tú ya resuelves el problema manualmente; el código solo vendría a replicar tu criterio a escala.

¿Eso se entiende o quieres que lo gire de otra forma?

Ejemplos prácticos: código vs terminal
Aquí van ejemplos concretos, mapeados a lo que tú haces:

Solo con / + prompt (sin código)
Situación	Qué haces
Analizas una letra y quieres la interpretación	Pegas la letra, pones tu / donde cambia el registro, le dices al LLM "sigue esta estructura y explica por qué funciona"
Comparas dos letras y quieres saber cuál es más efectiva	Pegas ambas, pones / en cada una, le pides al LLM que compare
Quieres que te sugiera qué viene en la línea 4 basándote en lo que ya analizaste de 1-3	Pegas tu análisis + las líneas, le pides "¿cuál es el resultado más probable?"
Quieres revisar si tu interpretación tiene sentido	Le pasas tu análisis completo y le dices "¿hay algo que no cuadre?"

Regla: si es una cosa a la vez, tú decides cuándo pasa cada cosa, y no necesitas guardar nada → no necesitas código.

Donde sí necesitas código
Situación	Por qué no basta con /
Tienes 50 letras de un álbum y quieres analizar todas con el mismo criterio	No vas a pegar 50 veces. Necesitas un loop que lea cada archivo, aplique tu prompt, y guarde el resultado
Quieres guardar tus análisis para luego decir "compara la línea 3 de esta canción con la línea 3 de aquella"	Sin base de datos (o al menos un JSON/CSV), cada análisis se pierde al cerrar la sesión
Quieres que el sistema detecte solo dónde poner el /	Eso es un agente. Necesitas código que llame al LLM, le pida "¿dónde cambia el registro?", y luego ejecute la interpretación
Quieres medir algo: "de 30 canciones, en cuántas la línea 3 es un statement vs una pregunta"	Eso es conteo + tabulación. Un script de 10 líneas en Python lo resuelve; a mano te toma una tarde
Quieres automatizar el flujo completo: pegar letra → detectar estructura → detectar emoción → interpretar → guardar	Eso es un pipeline. Sin código, tú eres el pipeline

La línea divisoria (en una frase)
Si puedes hacerlo en una sesión de chat sin que se te olvide nada, no necesitas código.
Si necesitas que algo pase de nuevo, a escala, o sin que tú estés ahí, necesitas código.

Tu / es la especificación. El código es la ejecución repetida de esa especificación. Mientras no repitas, no necesitas el segundo paso.

=== context\Notas\2026\Octubre\Nuevo Documento de texto.txt ===
import os
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

# Mapeo de extensión → carpeta destino
REGLAS = {
    ".pdf": "Documentos",
    ".txt": "Documentos",
    ".docx": "Documentos",
    ".jpg": "Imágenes",
    ".png": "Imágenes",
    ".mp3": "Audio",
    ".mp4": "Video",
    ".xlsx": "Hojas de cálculo",
}

def organizar(carpeta_fuente):
    """Mueve archivos de una carpeta a subcarpetas según su extensión."""
    fuente = Path(carpeta_fuente)
    movidos = 0

    for archivo in fuente.iterdir():
        if archivo.is_file():
            ext = archivo.suffix.lower()
            destino_carpeta = REGLAS.get(ext, "Otros")
            destino = fuente / destino_carpeta
            destino.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
            shutil.move(str(archivo), str(destino / archivo.name))
            movidos += 1

    print(f"Se movieron {movidos} archivos.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    carpeta = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."
    organizar(carpeta)

"""
pipeline_redes.py
Pipeline multi-agente para redes sociales.
Independiente de agentes.py — no lo modifica.

import os
import json
import time
import requests
import ollama

# ============================================================
# CONFIGURACIÓN
# ============================================================

OLLAMA_MODEL = "llama3.2"  # ← cambia por el que tengas

# Tokens (ponlos en .env o exportalos)
X_ACCESS_TOKEN = os.getenv("X_ACCESS_TOKEN", "")
FB_PAGE_ID = os.getenv("FB_PAGE_ID", "")
FB_PAGE_TOKEN = os.getenv("FB_PAGE_TOKEN", "")
IG_USER_ID = os.getenv("IG_USER_ID", "")
IG_ACCESS_TOKEN = os.getenv("IG_ACCESS_TOKEN", "")
TIKTOK_ACCESS_TOKEN = os.getenv("TIKTOK_ACCESS_TOKEN", "")

GRAPH_API = "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0"


# ============================================================
# FASE 1: RECOLECTOR — Obtiene datos de cada red
# ============================================================

def recolectar_x() -> dict:
    """Obtiene métricas básicas de tu cuenta en X."""
    if not X_ACCESS_TOKEN:
        return {"red": "X", "error": "Sin token"}
    try:
        # GET /2/users/me?user.fields=public_metrics
        r = requests.get(
            "https://api.twitter.com/2/users/me",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {X_ACCESS_TOKEN}"},
            params={"user.fields": "public_metrics"}
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        data = r.json()["data"]
        return {
            "red": "X",
            "seguidores": data.get("public_metrics", {}).get("followers_count", 0),
            "seguimientos": data.get("public_metrics", {}).get("following_count", 0),
            "tuits": data.get("public_metrics", {}).get("tweet_count", 0),
            "likes_recibidos": data.get("public_metrics", {}).get("like_count", 0),
        }
    except Exception as e:
        return {"red": "X", "error": str(e)}


def recolectar_facebook() -> dict:
    """Obtiene métricas de tu página de Facebook."""
    if not FB_PAGE_TOKEN:
        return {"red": "Facebook", "error": "Sin token"}
    try:
        r = requests.get(
            f"{GRAPH_API}/{FB_PAGE_ID}",
            params={
                "fields": "followers,likes,talk_about_count",
                "access_token": FB_PAGE_TOKEN
            }
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        data = r.json()
        return {
            "red": "Facebook",
            "seguidores": data.get("followers", 0),
            "me_gusta": data.get("likes", 0),
            "hablan_de": data.get("talk_about_count", 0),
        }
    except Exception as e:
        return {"red": "Facebook", "error": str(e)}


def recolectar_instagram() -> dict:
    """Obtiene métricas de tu cuenta de Instagram (Business/Creator)."""
    if not IG_ACCESS_TOKEN:
        return {"red": "Instagram", "error": "Sin token"}
    try:
        r = requests.get(
            f"{GRAPH_API}/{IG_USER_ID}",
            params={
                "fields": "followers_count,media_count",
                "access_token": IG_ACCESS_TOKEN
            }
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        data = r.json()
        return {
            "red": "Instagram",
            "seguidores": data.get("followers_count", 0),
            "publicaciones": data.get("media_count", 0),
        }
    except Exception as e:
        return {"red": "Instagram", "error": str(e)}


def recolectar_tiktok() -> dict:
    """Obtiene info básica de tu cuenta en TikTok."""
    if not TIKTOK_ACCESS_TOKEN:
        return {"red": "TikTok", "error": "Sin token"}
    try:
        r = requests.get(
            "https://open.tiktokapis.com/v2/user/info/?fields=[\"follower_count\",\"following_count\",\"video_count\",\"heart_count\"]",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TIKTOK_ACCESS_TOKEN}"}

            "seguidores": data.get("follower_count", 0),
            "videos": data.get("video_count", 0),
            "likes": data.get("heart_count", 0),
        }
    except Exception as e:

=== context\Notas\2026\Septiembre\`#` is the comment character in Pyt.txt ===
**`#`** is the **comment** character in Python. Everything after it on a line is ignored by the interpreter — it's just a note for humans reading the code.

```python
x = 10  # this is a comment, Python ignores it
print(x)  # prints 10
```

Use it to explain *why* you did something, not *what* (the code already shows *what*):

```python
# Convert to int because input() always returns a string
age = int(input("Age: "))
```

You can also comment out a line of code temporarily (to "disable" it without deleting it):

```python
# print("debug: x =", x)
```



=== context\Notas\2026\Septiembre\10 Tips for Writing System Prompts.txt ===
10 Tips for Writing System Prompts When AI Coding 

System prompt: text that gets prepended to every task you run it gives your aGENT EXTRA  context whoe you are how you like to code what level of explanation you want and how you want you´re Project structered 

Think of it like a "developer profile" that Sculpter uses behind the scenes every time you ask it to do something. 


Start with something like 

i´m a guy that would like to be a junior software engineer looking for a job or how to make a system of my own to make money, could you write high quality code but explain it like if i was a junior developer

Next clarify if your doing a quick prototype, or a production ready build. If you´re prototypeing, you can say:

Optimize for simplecity and speed of implementation. skip the tests and focus more on getting a working MVP 

If you´re productionizing, you can say: 

Write production grade code with full test coverage , robust error handling, and slean seperation of concerns.

This Will help Sculpter decide to scaffold out a quick demo or a fully stucterd Project. 

Next, add guidelines around how you want the code stucterd for example you can say 

Componentize UI elements wherever posible, Add to-do comments for unfinshed features, Document features with sconcise explanation, above each defination, follow clean code principles and consistent naming conventions. 
  
And the more you define your code filosfy the more Sculptor Will match your team´s actual style.

Next, sometimes have your goals have trade off´s for example speed verus memory usage. 

You can clarify, proiritize execution speed even if implemaentation is more complex or optimize for minimal storage usage even if it slightly increases runtime.

=== context\Notas\2026\Septiembre\Architecture Software patterns O`Reilly.md ===
# Architecture Software patterns 



## Introduction

It’s all too common for developers to start coding an application without a formal architecture in place. Without a clear and well-defined architecture, most developers and architects will resort to the de facto standard traditional layered architecture pattern (also called the n-tier architecture), creating implicit layers by separating source-code modules into packages. Unfortunately, what often results from this practice is a collection of unorganized source-code modules that lack clear roles, responsibilities, and relationships to one another. This is commonly referred to as the big ball of mud architecture anti-pattern. 



Applications lacking a formal architecture are generally tightly coupled, brittle, difficult to change, and without a clear vision or direction. As a result, it is very difficult to determine the architectural characteristics of the application without fully understanding the inner-workings of every component and module in the system. Basic questions about deployment and maintenance are hard to answer: Does the architecture scale? What are the performance characteristics of the application? How easily does the application respond to change? What are the deployment characteristics of the application? How responsive is the architecture? 



Architecture patterns help define the basic characteristics and behavior of an application. For example, some architecture patterns naturally lend themselves toward highly scalable applications, whereas other architecture patterns naturally lend themselves toward applications that are highly agile. Knowing the characteristics, strengths, and weaknesses of each architecture pattern is necessary in order to choose the one that meets your specific business needs and goals. 



As an architect, you must always justify your architecture decisions, particularly when it comes to choosing a particular architecture pattern or approach. The goal of this report is to give you enough information to make and justify that decision.





## Chapter 1. Layered Architecture

The most common architecture pattern is the layered architecture pattern, otherwise known as the n-tier architecture pattern. This pattern is the de facto standard for most Java EE applications and therefore is widely known by most architects, designers, and developers. The layered architecture pattern closely matches the traditional IT communication and organizational structures found in most companies, making it a natural choice for most business application development efforts. 



### Pattern Description

Components within the layered architecture pattern are organized into horizontal layers, each layer performing a specific role within the application (e.g., presentation logic or business logic). Although the layered architecture pattern does not specify the number and types of layers that must exist in the pattern, most layered architectures consist of four standard layers: presentation, business, persistence, and database (Figure 1-1). In some cases, the business layer and persistence layer are combined into a single business layer, particularly when the persistence logic (e.g., SQL or HSQL) is embedded within the business layer components. Thus, smaller applications may have only three layers, whereas larger and more complex business applications may contain five or more layers. 



Each layer of the layered architecture pattern has a specific role and responsibility within the application. For example, a presentation layer would be responsible for handling all user interface and browser communication logic, whereas a business layer would be responsible for executing specific business rules associated with the request. Each layer in the architecture forms an abstraction around the work that needs to be done to satisfy a particular business request. For example, the presentation layer doesn’t need to know or worry about how to get customer data; it only needs to display that information on a screen in particular format. Similarly, the business layer doesn’t need to be concerned about how to format customer data for display on a screen or even where the customer data is coming from; it only needs to get the data from the persistence layer, perform business logic against the data (e.g., calculate values or aggregate data), and pass that information up to the presentation layer.  



##### Alt Text

##### Figure 1-1. Layered architecture pattern

One of the powerful features of the layered architecture pattern is the separation of concerns among components. Components within a specific layer deal only with logic that pertains to that layer. For example, components in the presentation layer deal only with presentation logic, whereas components residing in the business layer deal only with business logic. This type of component classification makes it easy to build effective roles and responsibility models into your architecture, and also makes it easy to develop, test, govern, and maintain applications using this architecture pattern due to well-defined component interfaces and limited component scope.



##### Key Concepts

Notice in Figure 1-2 that each of the layers in the architecture is marked as being closed. This is a very important concept in the layered architecture pattern. A closed layer means that as a request moves from layer to layer, it must go through the layer right below it to get to the next layer below that one. For example, a request originating from the presentation layer must first go through the business layer and then to the persistence layer before finally hitting the database layer. 



##### Alt Text

##### Figure 1-2. Closed layers and request access

So why not allow the presentation layer direct access to either the persistence layer or database layer? After all, direct database access from the presentation layer is much faster than going through a bunch of unnecessary layers just to retrieve or save database information. The answer to this question lies in a key concept known as layers of isolation. 



The layers of isolation concept means that changes made in one layer of the architecture generally don’t impact or affect components in other layers: the change is isolated to the components within that layer, and possibly another associated layer (such as a persistence layer containing SQL). If you allow the presentation layer direct access to the persistence layer, then changes made to SQL within the persistence layer would impact both the business layer and the presentation layer, thereby producing a very tightly coupled application with lots of interdependencies between components. This type of architecture then becomes very hard and expensive to change.  



The layers of isolation concept also means that each layer is independent of the other layers, thereby having little or no knowledge of the inner workings of other layers in the architecture. To understand the power and importance of this concept, consider a large refactoring effort to convert the presentation framework from JSP (Java Server Pages) to JSF (Java Server Faces). Assuming that the contracts (e.g., model) used between the presentation layer and the business layer remain the same, the business layer is not affected by the refactoring and remains completely independent of the type of user-interface framework used by the presentation layer.  



While closed layers facilitate layers of isolation and therefore help isolate change within the architecture, there are times when it makes sense for certain layers to be open. For example, suppose you want to add a shared-services layer to an architecture containing common service components accessed by components within the business layer (e.g., data and string utility classes or auditing and logging classes). Creating a services layer is usually a good idea in this case because architecturally it restricts access to the shared services to the business layer (and not the presentation layer). Without a separate layer, there is nothing architecturally that restricts the presentation layer from accessing these common services, making it difficult to govern this access restriction.  



In this example, the new services layer would likely reside below the business layer to indicate that components in this services layer are not accessible from the presentation layer. However, this presents a problem in that the business layer is now required to go through the services layer to get to the persistence layer, which makes no sense at all. This is an age-old problem with the layered architecture, and is solved by creating open layers within the architecture.  



As illustrated in Figure 1-3, the services layer in this case is marked as open,  meaning requests are allowed to bypass this open layer and go directly to the layer below it. In the following example, since the services layer is open, the business layer is now allowed to bypass it and go directly to the persistence layer, which makes perfect sense.  



##### Alt Text

##### Figure 1-3. Open layers and request flow

Leveraging the concept of open and closed layers helps define the relationship between architecture layers and request flows and also provides designers and developers with the necessary information to understand the various layer access restrictions within the architecture. Failure to document or properly communicate which layers in the architecture are open and closed (and why) usually results in tightly coupled and brittle architectures that are very difficult to test, maintain, and deploy.



### Pattern Example

To illustrate how the layered architecture works, consider a request from a business user to retrieve customer information for a particular individual as illustrated in Figure 1-4. The black arrows show the request flowing down to the database to retrieve the customer data, and the red arrows show the response flowing back up to the screen to display the data. In this example, the customer information consists of both customer data and order data (orders placed by the customer).  



The customer screen is responsible for accepting the request and displaying the customer information. It does not know where the data is, how it is retrieved, or how many database tables must be queries to get the data. Once the customer screen receives a request to get customer information for a particular individual, it then forwards that request onto the customer delegate module. This module is responsible for knowing which modules in the business layer can process that request and also how to get to that module and what data it needs (the contract). The customer object in the business layer is responsible for aggregating all of the information needed by the business request (in this case to get customer information). This module calls out to the customer dao (data access object) module in the persistence layer to get customer data, and also the order dao module to get order information. These modules in turn execute SQL statements to retrieve the corresponding data and pass it back up to the customer object in the business layer. Once the customer object receives the data, it aggregates the data and passes that information back up to the customer delegate, which then passes that data to the customer screen to be presented to the user.      



##### Alt Text

##### Figure 1-4. Layered architecture example

From a technology perspective, there are literally dozens of ways these modules can be implemented. For example, in the Java platform, the customer screen can be a (JSF) Java Server Faces screen coupled with the customer delegate as the managed bean component. The customer object in the business layer can be a local Spring bean or a remote EJB3 bean. The data access objects illustrated in the previous example can be implemented as simple POJO’s (Plain Old Java Objects), MyBatis XML Mapper files, or even objects encapsulating raw JDBC calls or Hibernate queries. From a Microsoft platform perspective, the customer screen can be an ASP (active server pages) module using the .NET framework to access C# modules in the business layer, with the customer and order data access modules implemented as ADO (ActiveX Data Objects). 



###### Considerations

The layered architecture pattern is a solid general-purpose pattern, making it a good starting point for most applications, particularly when you are not sure what architecture pattern is best suited for your application. However, there are a couple of things to consider from an architecture standpoint when choosing this pattern.



The first thing to watch out for is what is known as the architecture sinkhole anti-pattern. This anti-pattern describes the situation where requests flow through multiple layers of the architecture as simple pass-through processing with little or no logic performed within each layer. For example, assume the presentation layer responds to a request from the user to retrieve customer data. The presentation layer passes the request to the business layer, which simply passes the request to the persistence layer, which then makes a simple SQL call to the database layer to retrieve the customer data. The data is then passed all the way back up the stack with no additional processing or logic to aggregate, calculate, or transform the data. 



Every layered architecture will have at least some scenarios that fall into the architecture sinkhole anti-pattern. The key, however, is to analyze the percentage of requests that fall into this category. The 80-20 rule is usually a good practice to follow to determine whether or not you are experiencing the architecture sinkhole anti-pattern. It is typical to have around 20 percent of the requests as simple pass-through processing and 80 percent of the requests having some business logic associated with the request. However, if you find that this ratio is reversed and a majority of your requests are simple pass-through processing, you might want to consider making some of the architecture layers open, keeping in mind that it will be more difficult to control change due to the lack of layer isolation. 



Another consideration with the layered architecture pattern is that it tends to lend itself toward monolithic applications, even if you split the presentation layer and business layers into separate deployable units. While this may not be a concern for some applications, it does pose some potential issues in terms of deployment, general robustness and reliability, performance, and scalability.   



#### Pattern Analysis

The following table contains a rating and analysis of the common architecture characteristics for the layered architecture pattern. The rating for each characteristic is based on the natural tendency for that characteristic as a capability based on a typical implementation of the pattern, as well as what the pattern is generally known for. For a side-by-side comparison of how this pattern relates to other patterns in this report, please refer to Appendix A at the end of this report.



#### Overall agility

Rating: Low

Analysis: Overall agility is the ability to respond quickly to a constantly changing environment. While change can be isolated through the layers of isolation feature of this pattern, it is still cumbersome and time-consuming to make changes in this architecture pattern because of the monolithic nature of most implementations as well as the tight coupling of components usually found with this pattern.

Ease of deployment

Rating: Low

Analysis: Depending on how you implement this pattern, deployment can become an issue, particularly for larger applications. One small change to a component can require a redeployment of the entire application (or a large portion of the application), resulting in deployments that need to be planned, scheduled, and executed during off-hours or on weekends. As such, this pattern does not easily lend itself toward a continuous delivery pipeline, further reducing the overall rating for deployment.

Testability

Rating: High

Analysis: Because components belong to specific layers in the architecture, other layers can be mocked or stubbed, making this pattern is relatively easy to test. A developer can mock a presentation component or screen to isolate testing within a business component, as well as mock the business layer to test certain screen functionality.

Performance

Rating: Low

Analysis: While it is true some layered architectures can perform well, the pattern does not lend itself to high-performance applications due to the inefficiencies of having to go through multiple layers of the architecture to fulfill a business request.

Scalability

Rating: Low

Analysis: Because of the trend toward tightly coupled and monolithic implementations of this pattern, applications build using this architecture pattern are generally difficult to scale. You can scale a layered architecture by splitting the layers into separate physical deployments or replicating the entire application into multiple nodes, but overall the granularity is too broad, making it expensive to scale.

Ease of development

Rating: High

Analysis: Ease of development gets a relatively high score, mostly because this pattern is so well known and is not overly complex to implement. Because most companies develop applications by separating skill sets by layers (presentation, business, database), this pattern becomes a natural choice for most business-application development. The connection between a company’s communication and organization structure and the way it develops software is 

outlined is what is called Conway’s law. You can Google “Conway’s law" to get more information about this fascinating correlation.





## Chapter 2. Event-Driven Architecture

The event-driven architecture pattern is a popular distributed asynchronous architecture pattern used to produce highly scalable applications. It is also highly adaptable and can be used for small applications and as well as large, complex ones. The event-driven architecture is made up of highly decoupled, single-purpose event processing components that asynchronously receive and process events. 



The event-driven architecture pattern consists of two main topologies, the mediator and the broker. The mediator topology is commonly used when you need to orchestrate multiple steps within an event through a central mediator, whereas the broker topology is used when you want to chain events together without the use of a central mediator. Because the architecture characteristics and implementation strategies differ between these two topologies, it is important to understand each one to know which is best suited for your particular situation.



### Mediator Topology

The mediator topology is useful for events that have multiple steps and require some level of orchestration to process the event. For example, a single event to place a stock trade might require you to first validate the trade, then check the compliance of that stock trade against various compliance rules, assign the trade to a broker, calculate the commission, and finally place the trade with that broker. All of these steps would require some level of orchestration to determine the order of the steps and which ones can be done serially and in parallel.  



There are four main types of architecture components within the mediator topology: event queues, an event mediator, event channels, and event processors. The event flow starts with a client sending an event to an event queue, which is used to transport the event to the event mediator. The event mediator receives the initial event and orchestrates that event by sending additional asynchronous events to event channels to execute each step of the process. Event processors, which listen on the event channels, receive the event from the event mediator and execute specific business logic to process the event. Figure 2-1 illustrates the general mediator topology of the event-driven architecture pattern. 



### Alt Text

### Figure 2-1. Event-driven architecture mediator topology

It is common to have anywhere from a dozen to several hundred event queues in an event-driven architecture. The pattern does not specify the implementation of the event queue component; it can be a message queue, a web service endpoint, or any combination thereof.

=== context\Notas\2026\Septiembre\C++.md ===
C++



Object-Oriented Design



Encapusulation: Hide data inside clases using private Access speecifiers 



Polymorphism: Use virtual functiond for Dynamic dispatch, but watch out for viable indierection overhead in tight loops.



Value Types: Perfer owning value types over complex refrence hierarchies to make object lifetimes predictable.







Memory Management



Smart Pointers: Use **std::unique\_ptr** when shared ownership is requiered. 



Manuel Control: Allocate and reléase dynamic memory saf etly using modern RAII(Resource Accquisition Is Initialized) patterns rather than raw **new** and **delete** calls.



Avoid Leaks: Design destructors properly---virtual destructores are requiered in base clases to prevent resources leaks during polymorphic deletion.





Performance Optimization 



Cache Efficency: Reserve vector capacities upfront and prefer flat data structures over fragmented pointer-heavy graphs.



Compile Time Polymorphism: Use templates instead of virtual functions in performance-critical sections to eliminate runtime dispatch costs. 



Non-Owning Views: **Pass std::stringview or std ::span** instead  of copying strings or containers in hot esecution paths

Dart \& Flutter Core Pillars 



Expert capability in Dart programming involves mastery of sound nulllsafety, asynchronous operations **with Future** and **Stream,** and multiplatform Flutter UI implementation  





1. Asynchronous Programming: Uses **async** and **await** syntactic sugar alongside **Future** for single operations and **Stream** for  data sequences. Concurrency is manged vía **isolates** to keep UIs running at high frame rates.
2. Sound Null Safety: Guarantees that variables cannot contain **null** unless explicitly marked with a question mark **(?)**, eliminating common runtime null-reference exceptions,
3. Declarative UI: employs a rich widget tree where the user interface updates automatically nased on application state transitions.

Import os
from contextlib import contextmanager
import psycopg
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from psycopg.rows import dict_row

load_dotenv()


def get_conninfo():
    return (
        f"host={os.getenv('DB_HOST', 'localhost')} "
        f"port={os.getenv('DB_PORT', '5432')} "
        f"dbname={os.getenv('DB_NAME', 'tienda')} "
        f"user={os.getenv('DB_USER', 'postgres')} "
        f"password={os.getenv('DB_PASSWORD', '')}"
    )


def get_connection():
    return psycopg.connect(get_conninfo(), row_factory=dict_row)

#### 

1. ###### Fundamentos de POO en C#,C++,CSS



Clases y Objetos: La plantilla (clase) y la instancia en memoria (objeto). Definición de propiedades, campos, métodos y constructores.



Encapsulamiento: Ocultar el estado interno usando modificadores de acceso (**private, protected, ublic, internal**) y esponerlo de forma segura mediante propiedades con **get y set.**  



Herencia: Reutilización de código permitiendo que una clase derive de otra (**classGerente : Empleado**). C# soporta herencia simple de clases.



Polimorfismo: Capacidad de un objeto de tomar muchas formas. Se logra mediante la sobreescritura de métodos (**virtual** y  **override**) y el uso de interfaces. 



Inerfaces y Clases Abstractas: Contratos de comportamientos **(interface)** frente a clases base parciales **( abstract class )** que no se pueden instanciar.







###### 2\. Caracteristicas Esenciales del Lenguaje



Colecciones Genéricas: Uso efficiente **de List<T**> para listas dinámicas **y Dictonary<TKey, TValuve**> para búsquedas rápidas basadas en clave-valor. 



LINQ (Language Integrated Query):Sintaxis podersa para filtrar, ordenar y transformar colecciones de datos (ej**. datos.where(x => x.Activo).Select(x =>x.Nombre) ).**



Tipos Nulos (Nullable types):Manejo seguro de la ausencia de valor mediante **Nullable<T**> o el operador simplificado **?** (ej. int? edad = null; ), crucial para evitar el famoso error **NullreferenceException.** 



Manejo de Excepciones: Control de erroes en tiempo de ejecución utilizado **bloques  try,catch** y **finally** ,junto con la creación de excepciones personalizadas.  



###### 3\. Conceptos Avanzados y Rendimiento 



Prohramación Asincrona (**asyn / await)**: Liberación del hilo principal para mejorar la escalabilidad de las aplicaciones, especialesmente en operaciones de entrada/salida (I/O) como consultas a bases de datos o APIs.



Gestión de Memoria (Garbage Collection): Entender cómo funciona el recolectar de basura de .NET, la diferencia entre el Stack (valores) y el Heap (referencias). y la implementación de la interfaz **IDisposible** (bloques **using** ) para liberar recursos no administrados.



Arquitectura Limpia (Clean Architecture): Organización del proyecto en capas desacopladas (Dominio, Aplicación, Infraestructura, Presentación) para garantizar que la lógica de negocio sea independiente de las bases de datos, framework, y la interfaz usario.









=== context\Notas\2026\Septiembre\Docker.md ===
Docker is a tool that solves the classic develper problema: "It worked on my machine, but it dosen´t work in production." It does this by wrapping a piece of software and everything it needs to run into a neat, ioslated package called a container.HERE is step-by-step roadmap to help you undersatnd and master Docker from scratch.1\. The Core Concepts(The "Why" and "What")Before writing any code, it helps to understand the three main pillars of Docker:The Container: Think of this as a leightweight, isolated virtual box.Inside this box is your application (e.g., a Python script or a website) and all the tolos it needs to run.The image: This is the blueprint or récipe used to créate the container. If a container is a baked cake, the image is the récipe.The Docker file: A simple text file containing the exact instructions on how to build your Docker Image.2\. A 3-Step Learning RoadmapPhase 1: The Basics (Week 1)Install Docker DEsktop: Download it on your Mac, Windows, or Linux machine.**Docker run hello-world** (Downloads and runs atest container)**Docker ps** (Lists your running containers)**Docker stop** \[container\_id] (Stops a running container)Phase 2: Building Your Own (Week 2)Write a Dockerfile: Take a simple application you´ve already built (like a basic HTML website or a simple Node/Python scipt) and write a Dockerfilefor it.Build an Image: Use the **Docker build** command to turn your Dockerfile into a reuseable image.Run Your App: Use **Docker run** to launch your own application inside a container.Phase 3: Advanced Concepts (Week 3+)Docker Compose: Learn how to use a tool called Docker Compose to run multiple containers at the same time (for example, running a WordPress website in one container and a MySQL database in another container, and making them talk to each other).Volumes: Learn how to sabe data so it doesn´t disappear when a container is deletedRecommended Free ResourcesOfficial Docker Guides: The Docker Getting Started guide is excellent and interactive.YouTube Creators: Look up "Docker Beginner Tutorial" by creaters like TechWorld with Nana or NetworkChunk. They explain things using great visual analogies.Interactive Labs: Websites like Play with Docker let you practice Docker directly in your web browser without installing anythingDocker getting started guidehttps://www.google.com/url?sa=i\&source=web\&rct=j\&url=https://docs.docker.com/get-started/\&ved=2ahUKEwjNyuWdvuiWAxWDCoYAHaJRANkQy\_kOegYIAAgXEAI\&opi=89978449\&cd\&psig=AOvVaw1zm4cQS23zgI40jJqbnPm4\&ust=1789283401823000Play with Dockerhttps://www.google.com/url?sa=i\&source=web\&rct=j\&url=https://labs.play-with-docker.com/\&ved=2ahUKEwjNyuWdvuiWAxWDCoYAHaJRANkQy\_kOegYIAAgXEAU\&opi=89978449\&cd\&psig=AOvVaw1zm4cQS23zgI40jJqbnPm4\&ust=1789283401823000

-- Tienda online — modelo de datos mínimo
-- Motor: PostgreSQL 14+
-- Si usas MySQL 8, ves las notas al final.

CREATE TABLE usuarios (
    id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    nombre          VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    email           VARCHAR(180) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash   VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    telefono        VARCHAR(30),
    creado_en       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE direcciones (
    id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    usuario_id      BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES usuarios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    calle           VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    ciudad          VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    codigo_postal   VARCHAR(20),
    pais            VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'México',
    es_principal    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE
);

CREATE TABLE productos (
    id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    nombre          VARCHAR(160) NOT NULL,
    descripcion     TEXT,
    precio          NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (precio >= 0),
    stock           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (stock >= 0),
    activo          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    imagen_url      VARCHAR(500),
    creado_en       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE carrito_items (
    id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    usuario_id      BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES usuarios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    producto_id     BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES productos(id),
    cantidad        INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (cantidad > 0),
    agregado_en     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE (usuario_id, producto_id)
);

CREATE TABLE pedidos (
    id                BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    usuario_id        BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES usuarios(id),
    estado            VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pendiente'
                      CHECK (estado IN ('pendiente', 'pagado', 'fallido', 'enviado', 'cancelado')),
    total             NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (total >= 0),
    direccion_envio   VARCHAR(300) NOT NULL,
    creado_en         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE pedido_items (
    id               BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    pedido_id        BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES pedidos(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    producto_id      BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES productos(id),
    cantidad         INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (cantidad > 0),
    precio_unitario  NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (precio_unitario >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE pagos (
    id                   BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    pedido_id            BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES pedidos(id),
    proveedor            VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    referencia_externa   VARCHAR(120),
    monto                NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (monto >= 0),
    estado               VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pendiente'
                         CHECK (estado IN ('pendiente', 'ok', 'fallido')),
    creado_en            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_direcciones_usuario ON direcciones(usuario_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_carrito_usuario     ON carrito_items(usuario_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_pedidos_usuario     ON pedidos(usuario_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_pedido_items_pedido ON pedido_items(pedido_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_pagos_pedido        ON pagos(pedido_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_productos_activo    ON productos(activo);

-- Datos de prueba opcionales
INSERT INTO productos (nombre, descripcion, precio, stock, activo)
VALUES
    ('Playera básica', 'Algodón, talla única de muestra', 199.00, 25, TRUE),
    ('Gorra', 'Gorra de gabardina', 149.00, 10, TRUE);

/*
MySQL 8 — cambios:
  BIGSERIAL          → BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT
  TIMESTAMPTZ        → DATETIME(3)
  BOOLEAN            → TINYINT(1)
  DEFAULT NOW()      → DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)
  Quita CHECK si tu versión se queja; en MySQL 8.0.16+ sí existen.
*/

=== context\Notas\2026\Septiembre\GO.md ===
GO 



is famous dir its concurrency model, which is built into the language rather than treated as an afterthought. Advanced expertise means knowing how to write safe, highly scalable code.



Goroutines \& Channels: You must understand how the Go Runtim Scheduler manages thousand f goroutines multiplexed onto a small number of OS threads (the M:N scheduler). Master unbuffered vs. buffered channels and how to close channels safely.



Concurrency Patterns: Learn standard patterns like Worker Pools, Pieplines, Fan-out/Fan-in, and the Context package (context.ContextN ) for handling cancellations signals and timeouts across API boundries. 



Memory Synchrounization: Whilw Go favores 2communicating by sharing memory", you still need to know when to use the sync package. Master sync.Mutex, sync.RWMutex, sync.WaitGroup, sync.Once, and the sync/atomic package for look-free operations. 



Race Conditions:You must know how to detect and prevent data races using Go´s built-in race detector. 





Systems Devolpement 



Systems Devolpemnet involves building low-lvl high performance in¿frastructure like network services,data base and microservice frameworks.



Networking (net package): Understand how to build low-level TCP/UDP servers and handles raw network sockets. You should also be highly profecient with gRPC and Prtocol Buffers (protobuf) for high\_performance microservice communication.



Linux/OS Interactions: Learn how Go interacts with the operating systems. This includes handling OS signals, working with the filesytem efficiently and using the syscall or  golang.org/x/sys packages for direct system calls.



I/O Efficency: Master the io.Reader and io.Writer interfaces. Understand how to use buffered I/O(bufio package) to minimize expensive system calls when Reading or writing data.  



Performance Optimization \& Tools



Advanced Go developers don´t guess why code is slow; they measure it. You need to understand Go´s Internals to squeeze out maxium performance.



Memory Manegement: Learn how GO allocates nenory, underatnd Escape Analysis (how the complier decide if a variable goes on the fast stack or the slow heap).



Garbage Collection /GC): Go´s GC is optimized for low latency. You need to know how to write GC-friendly code by minimizing heap allocations, using sync.Pool to reuse object, and understandinghow the GOGC tuning variable works.



Profiling (pprof): Master the **runtime/pprof and net/http/pprof** packages. You should be able to read CPU profiles, Memory (healp) profiles, and Block/Mutex profiles to find bottlenecks.



Benchmarking: Learn hoe to wrtie rigorous benchmarks using the **texting** package **(go test -Bench**) and interpret the sesults (e.g., ns/op, B/op, aloocs/op).



THE ADVANCED GO TECH STACK \& BEST PRACTICES 



Familiarize yourself with the tolos and standards the industry expects:





|CATEGORY|                       Tools \& Concepts to Master|
|-|-|
|||
|LINTERNS \& FORMATTERS|**gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint** (the industry standard meta-linter).|
|DEPENDENCY<br />MANAGEMENT|Go modules ( **go.mod, go.sum** ), vendoring and proxy configuaration. |
|PROJECT ARCHITECTURE|Standard Go Project Layout (e.g., **/cmd, /internal, /pkg**) and Clean Arquitecture/DDD principals.|
|OBSERVABILITY|Integrating OpenTelementry, Prometheus metricx, and structured logging (**slog package**)|



Remcommended Road Maps to Learn This



Since you have time to learn, here is the best sequence to approach these topics:



Read the go programming language by alan donovan and brain Kerighan. It is the defentive guide for Deep foundational mechanics.



Study Go Internals: Read articals on how the Go Scheduler Works and how Go maps/slices are structured under the Hood 



Build a Systems Project: Don´t just build a standard web app. Build something complaex from scratc, like a custome redis-clone, a distributaed key-store, or a concurrent web scraperusing worker pools.



Profile Your Project: Take yoyr Project, run a load tester aganist it, use **pprof** to find the slowest funtions, and rewrite them to use fewer memory allocations.

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPExceptionfrom db import get_connection
app = FastAPI(title="Tienda API", version="0.1.0")

@app.get("/salud")def salud():    with get_connection() as conn:        conn.execute("SELECT 1")    return {"ok": True, "db": "tienda"}

@app.get("/productos")def listar_productos():    with get_connection() as conn:        filas = conn.execute(            """            SELECT id, nombre, descripcion, precio, stock, activo, imagen_url            FROM productos            WHERE activo = TRUE            ORDER BY id            """        ).fetchall()    return [        {            "id": f["id"],            "nombre": f["nombre"],            "descripcion": f["descripcion"],            "precio": float(f["precio"]),            "stock": f["stock"],            "activo": f["activo"],            "imagen_url": f["imagen_url"],        }        for f in filas    ]

@app.get("/productos/{producto_id}")def obtener_producto(producto_id: int):    with get_connection() as conn:        fila = conn.execute(            """            SELECT id, nombre, descripcion, precio, stock, activo, imagen_url            FROM productos            WHERE id = %s            """,            (producto_id,),        ).fetchone()    if fila is None:        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Producto no encontrado")    return {        "id": fila["id"],        "nombre": fila["nombre"],        "descripcion": fila["descripcion"],        "precio": float(fila["precio"]),        "stock": fila["stock"],        "activo": fila["activo"],        "imagen_url": fila["imagen_url"],    }

For more official guidance on navigating these structures, read the Microsoft Learn Registry Guide for Advanced Users. [1] (https://learn.microsoft.com/es-es/troubleshoot/windows-server/performance/windows-registry-advanced-users)





What is HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE used for?
Visión general creada por IA
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (often abbreviated as HKLM) is a primary root key in the Windows Registry that stores computer-wide configuration settings, hardware data, and software options shared by all users. 

YouTube
·ThioJoe
 +2
Core Uses of HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Hardware Configurations: Stores information regarding physical components, device drivers, and Plug and Play settings detected by the system under subkeys like HARDWARE and DRIVERS. 

Lifewire
 +1
System Boot and Control: Retains crucial startup parameters, kernel configurations, and Windows services data under subkeys like SYSTEM. 

Medium
·Shlomi Boutnaru, Ph.D.
 +1
Installed Software Settings: Holds machine-wide application settings, file associations, and paths under the SOFTWARE subkey, applying to every user account on the machine. 

Reddit
·r/windows
 +2
Security and Accounts: Manages local security policies, user account information, and access control lists via hidden or restricted subkeys like SAM and SECURITY. 

Wikipedia
 +1
Read more about advanced management in the Microsoft Learn Registry Guide. 




What does the HKEY_CURRENT_USER hive in the Windows Registry Store?
Visión general creada por IA
The HKEY_CURRENT_USER (HKCU) hive stores configuration and preference data specific to the user currently logged into the Windows system. 

Microsoft Learn
 +1
What It Stores
Desktop Preferences: Screen colors, window sizes, and desktop wallpaper settings.
Control Panel Settings: Personalizations, mouse configurations, and accessibility choices.
Application Settings: Software preferences, user-specific program configurations, and recent file lists for apps tied to the user account.
Environment & Connections: Network connections, mapped drives, and installed printers. 

Microsoft Learn
 +3
How It Works
Active Link: HKCU acts as a dynamic pointer or shortcut to the specific user profile section located inside HKEY_USERS (specifically matching that user's Security ID or SID).
Physical File: The data displayed in this hive maps directly to the NTUSER.DAT file found inside the profile folder of the active user (C:\Users\<Username>). 

Reddit
·r/sysadmin
 +2




In which registry hive does Windows store files a user has recently accessed?
Visión general creada por IA
Windows stores recently accessed files and user activity in the NTUSER.DAT registry hive (mapped live as HKEY_CURRENT_USER). 

Cyber Triage
 +1
Location and Path
On-Disk File Path: C:\Users\<Username>\NTUSER.DAT
Registry Path: Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RecentDocs 

Course Hero
 +1
Key Artifacts for Recently Accessed Files
Within the NTUSER.DAT hive, Windows tracks file access through specific subkeys (often called MRU or Most Recently Used lists):
RecentDocs: Tracks general files opened by the user, broken down by file extension.
OpenSaveMRU: Records the last files opened or saved using standard dialog boxes per file extension.
LastVisitedMRU: Tracks folders and paths recently accessed by applications. 

Cyber Triage
 +1



How to remove the registry of uninstalled programs?
Visión general creada por IA
To remove registry entries for uninstalled software, you can manually delete them using the built-in Registry Editor or use a specialized third-party uninstaller.
Back Up the Registry First
Always create a backup before changing the registry. A mistake can cause system errors. 

Microsoft Community Hub
 +1
Press Win + R, type regedit, and press Enter.
Click File and then Export.
Choose All for the export range, name the file, and save it. 

Microsoft Community Hub
Method 1: Manually Search and Delete Leftovers
Open the Registry Editor by typing regedit in the Run window (Win + R).
Press Ctrl + F to open the Find menu.
Type the name of the uninstalled software and click Find Next.
Carefully verify that the highlighted key belongs to the uninstalled program (check the publisher or folder name).
Right-click the key and select Delete.
Press F3 to search for the next matching entry and repeat the deletion. 

Blackview Official Store
 +1
Method 2: Clean the Uninstall List
If the program still shows up in your system's app list even though it is removed:
Open regedit.
Navigate to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall (and check HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall on 64-bit systems).
Look through the subkeys on the left and check the DisplayName or UninstallString on the right to identify the residual entry.
Right-click the key and select Delete. 

Stack Overflow
 +2
Method 3: Use Third-Party Uninstallers
If manual deletion feels too complicated or risky, you can use specialized tools like Revo Uninstaller or Bulk Crap Uninstaller. These tools automatically scan for and safely remove leftover files and registry traces after an app is uninstalled.




How can I delete a registry key that cannot be deleted?
Visión general creada por IA
To delete a stubborn registry key in Windows, you usually need to change its ownership and permissions. 

Super User
 +2
Change Ownership and Permissions
Open the Start menu, type regedit, and press Enter.
Find the key you want to delete.
Right-click the key and select Permissions.
Click the Advanced button.
Next to the owner name at the top, click Change.
Type Administrators (or your user name) in the box, click Check Names, and click OK.
Check the box that says Replace owner on subcontainers and objects. Click Apply.
Select Full Control for the Administrators group or Everyone, then click OK.
Try deleting the key again.

·Stefan Van Damme

   LEADER ELECTION

Process by which a group of nodes in a distributed system selects a single leader among them to coordinate and manage the system´s activities

 
  LEADER RESPONSIBILITIES

Resource ALlocation
Tasks Schedulling
Distributed Algorithms Coordination

Leader algorithms ensure that there Will always be a single leader even in case of failure or network partitions

Leader elections with RAFT
There are serveral other algorithms like Paxos and ZAB

Raft is used in multiple systems like Kafka, etcd and MongoDB.

In raft everyone starts in a follwer state

If there is no leader everyone can shout their name and term
(ej.. Chris!, 1er Term!) this is known as (Candidate State)

If oyu hear someone else´s name and term you vote for them indicating the name and term you Heard.

If a majority agrees, that one becomes the leader. if not, a new term starts.

The leader keeps everyone updated with im ok heart beats.

If this is stoped a new election is triggered.

All changes to the system are now done through the leader.

It´s not just impotant that everyone agrees to the new leader but that ALL THE NODES AGREE as well. we need CONSENSUS

CONSENSUS

Consensus is the process by which a group of a nodes in a distributed system agree on a single value or decisión despite the potential for failures or inconsistencies

This is often used to make sure that all nodes reach an agreement on critcal descions such as: committing a transaction, chosing a configuration option, or agreeing on a specific value.

CONSENSUS ALGORITHMS typically require processes to communicate to propose and agree on values while also ensuring properties like SAFETY and LIVENESS

SAFETY PROPERTY

the safety property of a systems means that it guarantees certain bad things wont happening (say all nodes agree on the same value) there Will be no disagreements

LIVENESS PROPERTY

Liveness is Good things Will happen (say, eventually all nodes agree on the same value)

CONSENSUS is not only relevant for Leader/node election but also for Data replicating

This consensus ensures data repilcation is reliable for example aslo in our picture sharing app


DATA REPLICATION WITH RAFT

Raft´s main use case is data replication it uses the concept of a state machine where all of the nodes start in the same state and by applying the same operations, in the same order, they all end up in the same state.

Each node in the system has a log of operations and a state which includes the actual data. WHen a client sends a request to store a file the leader adds this entry to his own log first before actually changing the state.

The leader then sends an AppendEntries message to all folower nodes which includes the new log entry.

Each follwer appends the receipt entry to its own log and sends an acknowledgement back to the leader.

Once the leader receives acknowledgement from a mjority of followers, it commits the entry.

COMMITTING
Means the entry is applied to the leader´s state.

For example, the file is saved.

Then the leader sends a message to the followers indicating the entry is comitted.

Followers then apply the entry to their own state.

This process ensures that all nodes maintain the same sequence of operations in their logs leading to a consistent state across the system.

Since we depend on the majority, several of the followers can fail and still work.

In Fact
Of we have 2F+1 followers up to F followers can fail.

When the leader fails, a new election is triggered.

and the new leader is chosen based on the highest log index to ensure no data is lost.

The new leader then continues to replicate entries from where the old leader left off.

IF A FOLLOWER FAILS

the leader Will keep on sending the appendEntries indefinitely until it gets confirmation.


Most of the times we won´t need the RAFT, nor nosensus, or leader election since other softwares cover that for you

also CALM THEOREM can be very helpful not covered today tho

In practice, only electing a leader to perform one action can be solved more easily by getting a lease or a lock with the time to live TTL for example using a

KEY VALUE STORE w/ ATOMIC COMPARE & SWAP SUPPORT

=== context\Notas\2026\Septiembre\Objetivo NENIS, Nuevas Empresarias.md ===
Objetivo: NENIS, Nuevas Empresarias con Negocios en Internet.



Impacto Economico: Hay mas de 1.2 millones de nenis las cuales generan ingresos multimillonarios fundamentales para la economía



Utilizan plataformas com Facebook Market PLace, Whatsapp, Instagram



Cordinan Entregas en puntos intermedios accesibles, como estaciones de metro o plazas publicas.



Retos:Enfrentan desafíos como la informalidad, la exclusión de servicios financieros tradicionales y la carga de doble jornada lobaral y familiar





Las Emprendedoras que operan bajo este modelo enfrentan barrearas operativas muy especificas, pero

La Pagina Web es una herramienta ideal para superar estos retos, automatizar el negocio y proyectar una imagen profesional.





#### Reto Operativo Tradicional					    Solución con una Pagína Web



|Perdida de tiempo en chat: Pasar horas respondiendo "precio", "tallas disponibles" o "puntos de entrega" por DM o WhastApp.|Catalogo Automatizado: El cliente ve inventario real, precios, tallas y descripción del producto 24/7 sin que tengas que responder un solo mensaje.|
|-|-|
|Entregas inseguras o difíciles: Cordinar horarios en estaciones del metro o plazas, con el reisgo de que el cliente mo llegue o exitan problemas de seguridad.|Envios integrados: Cobro automatico de guias de envió (Estafeta, DHL, Wolox, etc.) a domicilio o puntos de recolección (Lockers, tienda locales).|
|Desconfianzas del cliente: El miedo de los compradores a ser estafados al depositar a cuentas personales antes de recibir el producto.|Pasarelas de pago seguras: Ofrecer pagos con tarjetas, PayPal, Mercado Pago o SPEI, Esto da certeza legal y protege el dinero de ambas partes.|
|Falta de orden financiero: Llevar el registro de ventas, apartados y ganancias en libretas, lo que facilita los errores humanos.|Administración centralizada: El sistema web genera el stock automáticamente y te dice exactamente que se vendío.|
|Dependecia del algoritmo: Si Facebook o Instagram tiran tu cuenta, el negocio desaparece por completo de la noche a la mañana.|Canal propio e independiente: Tu web es tu propiedad digital. Los clientes te encuentran directo en Google y puedes crear bases de datos de correos para revenderles.|





###### Formalizacion gradual: Al contralizar los pagos en una plataforma web, se vuelve mucho mas fácil conectar las ventas con herramientas de facturación básica. Esto ayuda a cumplir con los retos FISCALES de forma ordenada y sin miedo al SAT.





LAS LETRAS CHIQUITAS Y COSTOS OCULTOS QUE DEBES CONSIDERAR



Al tener en linea, el costio mensual del plan es solo una parte de le ecuación, Considera estos tres puntos clave antes de decidir:



Comiciones Bancarias (Pasarelas de Pago): Independientementa de la plataforma, cuando un cliente paga con tarjeta, la pasarela de pagos (como Mercado Pago, Stripe o PayPal) cobra una taza aproximada del 3.4% al 3.9% + $3 o $4 MXN por cada transacción.



La Doble Comisión de Shopify: Si en Shopify decides usar una pasarela externa (como Mercado Pago) en lugar de su procesador nativo, Shopify te cobrara un 2% adicional sobre la venta en su plan básico.

Tienda nube no hace esto.



Promociones de Entrada: Ambas opciones suelen ofrecer incentivos atractivos para nuevos usarios. Por ejemplo,





lunaboutique.mx/p/chamarra?src=wa/ig/vipPrenda que vieron,/ si armaron carrito,/ pedido (nombre, Whatsapp, colonia, talla, color, estado.



Las Preferencias salen de pedidods reales: talla, colores, colonia, ticket.

Y lo mejor qunque no pilsen enviar el pedido ya esta en el panel/información ya esta guardada y prefrencias empiezan a guardarse/generarse

=== context\Notas\2026\Septiembre\POO.txt ===
La Programción Oriendtada a Objetos (POO) es un paradigma de programación que organiza el diseño de software alrededor de objetos y datos en lugar de funciones y lógica pura.

CONCEPTOS CLAVE 

Clase: Una plantilla o molde que define los atributos y los métodos comunes para crear objetos. 

Objeto: Una instancia concreta de una define los atributos y los métodos comunes para crear objetos.

Atributo: Las características o variables que almacenan el estado de un objeto. 

Método: Las funciones o acciones que el objeto puede realizar. 


LOS CUATRO PILLARES 

Encapsulamiento: Oculta los detalles internos del estado de un objeto para proteger los datos.  

Herencia: Permite que una clase nueva reciba atributos métodos de otra clase existente.

Polimorfismo: Permite que un mismo método actúe de formas distintas según el objeto que lo invoque. 

Abstracción: Modela solamente las características esenciales de un objeto ignorando detalles complejos. 

 

=== context\Notas\2026\Septiembre\Proyecto numero 1 e iniciación del soift ware.txt ===
Proyecto numero 1 e iniciación del software 


¡Es una excelente iniciativa! Construir proyectos reales con clientes y problemas verdaderos es la mejor forma de destacar en tu currículum (resume) como ingeniero de software. Los reclutadores valoran mucho más un producto que se está usando en el mundo real que un proyecto escolar de práctica.Aquí tienes el análisis de si es una buena idea para tu currículum y los pasos legales clave para la página web:¿Es un buen proyecto para presentar en tu Resume?Sí, es un proyecto sobresaliente, pero con una advertencia importante.Desde el punto de vista técnico, es fantástico. Un e-commerce o plataforma de cadena de suministro (conectar cultivadores, tiendas y proveedores de semillas) demuestra que dominas:Gestión de bases de datos complejas (inventarios, usuarios, roles de tienda vs. cultivador).Pasarelas de pago y seguridad (encriptación, manejo de transacciones).Sistemas de autenticación (verificación de edad estricta).⚠️ El único riesgo es el estigma cultural: Dependiendo del país o la empresa a la que postules (por ejemplo, empresas muy corporativas, financieras o en lugares donde la planta es ilegal), el tema del cannabis puede generar sesgos en algunos reclutadores.El truco para tu currículum: Si notas resistencia o quieres ir a la segura, puedes redactar el proyecto enfocado puramente en la arquitectura técnica. En lugar de llamarlo "Plataforma de Cannabis", puedes titularlo: "Plataforma B2B/B2C de E-commerce y Gestión de Cadena de Suministro para Productos Agrícolas de Alta Regulación". Técnicamente es 100% real y suena extremadamente profesional.Aspectos legales para construir la página webEl comercio de cannabis (incluso de semillas o accesorios) está fuertemente regulado en internet. Para cubrirte la espalda legalmente en la web, debes asegurar estos tres pilares:1. Verificación de Edad Estricta (Age Gating)No basta con un botón simple de "Soy mayor de edad". Necesitas implementar un sistema que obligue al usuario a confirmar su fecha de nacimiento e idealmente, dependiendo de las leyes de tu país local, integrar APIs de verificación de identidad para asegurarte de que no estás vendiendo ni mostrando contenido a menores.2. Pasarelas de Pago (El mayor reto)Las pasarelas de pago tradicionales como Stripe, PayPal o Shopify Payments suelen prohibir estrictamente los productos relacionados con el cannabis, semillas o parafernalia (incluso si es legal en tu estado o país).Solución: Deberás buscar procesadores de pago específicos para industrias de "alto riesgo" (High-Risk Merchant Accounts) o evaluar el uso de métodos alternativos (transferencias electrónicas SPEI/bancarias, pagos contra entrega o criptomonedas si el mercado lo adopta).3. Términos, Condiciones y Deslindes de Responsabilidad (Disclaimer)Tu web debe tener páginas legales obligatorias redactadas (de preferencia) por un abogado:Términos de Servicio: Especificar que la plataforma solo facilita la conexión o venta bajo los marcos legales locales.Política de Privacidad: Al manejar datos de clientes en esta industria, el cumplimiento de leyes de privacidad de datos (como la LFPDPPP en México o GDPR/CCPA si aplica) es crítico.Aviso de legalidad de semillas: En muchos países, las semillas se pueden vender como "artículos de colección" o souvenirs siempre y cuando no se germinen abiertamente fuera del marco legal. Debes dejar esto claro en los textos de la web.Próximos pasos recomendadosPara avanzar, lo ideal es separar el proyecto físico (el cultivo y las smoke shops de tus amigos) de tu rol como ingeniero de software. Tu enfoque principal debe ser el código y la arquitectura del sistema.Para ayudarte a estructurar mejor el proyecto para tu currículum, cuéntame:¿En qué país o región planeas operar legalmente el proyecto?¿Qué tecnologías o lenguajes de programación (por ejemplo: React, Node.js, Python, bases de datos SQL) te gustaría utilizar o aprender con esto?
